_comment: OpenTelemetry (OTel) configuration — issue #5081 (S1) + #5138 (destination switches) + #5082 (S2 metrics) + #2808 (S3 traces), observability program #5080. The single externalized source for every OTel switch. No module hard-codes an OTel value; change this file (or the matching env var) to change behavior, then update the pins in tests/otel_config_5081.test.ts and tests/otel_destinations_5138.test.ts that quote the value. Resolution order (the PAYMENTS_FLOW_MODE pattern): run > session > user > env > this file > built-in safe default (all OFF / none / 0). The built-in safe default applies only when this file is missing or a value is invalid; an invalid value fails closed to OFF with a coded OBS-1001 message and does NOT fall through. destinations: one switch per destination (Analytics Engine sink, R2 OTLP export, console sink) — all ON here, preserving the current behavior; each is individually flippable via its OTEL_DESTINATION_<NAME>_ENABLED env var. Workers Logs is NOT a switch in this file: it is deploy-time only, wrangler.jsonc observability.enabled (set false to silence it entirely; currently true at 1% sampling, persist false per #4131). The Worker cannot flip the Cloudflare platform log pipeline at runtime — no runtime switch exists for it, and none is pretended here. S2 (#5082): metricsExporter is otlp (the live signal now); the metrics section carries the export interval (60000ms), the Analytics Engine free-tier limits (100k writes/day, 10k read queries/day — config values, not hard-coded), the pipeline health max failure rate (0.05), and the resource SLO max pct (0.7). The metrics ingestion route is /api/otel/v1/metrics (same token gate as the logs route). S3 (#2808): tracesExporter is otlp (the live signal now); the traces section carries the Analytics Engine free-tier daily write limit (100k writes/day — a config value, not hard-coded); the traces ingestion route is /api/otel/v1/traces (same token gate as the logs/metrics routes). S4 (#5083): the alerting section carries the error-reporting switches — master enabled, Slack + email each individually on/off (both ON: every alert goes to both, Slack via SCREENER_SLACK_CHANNEL, email via CHANNEL_EMAIL_PRINCIPALS), and the free-tier guard maxAlertsPerDay (100/day, a config value, not hard-coded). Alerting credentials (SLACK_BOT_TOKEN / SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL) come from GitHub secrets (Worker secrets), never from this file. The CI failure alert ingestion route is /api/otel/v1/alerts (same OTEL_INGEST_TOKEN gate as the OTLP routes). S10 (#5164): the backend section carries the Grafana Cloud switch — enabled false (the default: telemetry stays on the free-tier path until the owner sets the one Worker secret and flips the switch), the OTLP request timeout (10000ms), the service name (ai-search-agent, the Worker name, stamped as service.name on every signal's OTLP resource), the wire protocol (http/json — the implemented serialization; http/protobuf is the portal default but is NOT implemented, and selecting it is a documented follow-up, not a silent switch), the gateway endpoint (https://otlp-gateway-prod-us-east-2.grafana.net/otlp, region us-east-2, from the portal Connections → OpenTelemetry) and the stack/instance ID (1929738). The endpoint + instance ID are config values, not secrets (owner direction 2026-11-22); only the API key (GRAFANA_CLOUD_API_KEY, scopes metrics:write, logs:write, traces:write) comes from a Worker secret, never from this file.
